note: A blank field means nobody has verified it yet. It does not mean no. This matters most for hazards and dams.
sources: Lower Haw River State Natural Area

spots.name: Anderson Point Access
spots.managing_agency: City of Raleigh Parks, Recreation and Cultural Resources
spots.parking_spaces: Small car park before the bridge, then a gravel road to the river
spots.restrooms: Yes, but three quarters of a mile to a mile away inside Anderson Point Park
spots.hours: Sunrise to sunset. No overnight parking, cars may not be left overnight.
spots.hazards: Fast current can push you into downed trees, log jams and bridge footings. The bed is uneven, so never stand where the water is deep enough to float you. Avoid the river in high flow.
spots.notes_public: River mile 16.2. The restrooms are a long walk from the water, so plan accordingly. Only 1.5 miles down to Poole Road, which makes this a short, easy pairing.

spots.name: Badin Lake Boat Ramp
spots.restrooms: Portable toilet only, no trash cans on site
spots.notes_public: Badin Lake sits in the Uwharrie National Forest and is the most scenic flatwater in the Piedmont Triad region. The dock sits some distance from the ramps, so a second person on the boat helps with loading. Paddle north into wooded coves away from the ramp for the best scenery. Popular at night — paddlers report the parking lot has lights and the lake is quiet after dark.

spots.name: Bass Lake Park
spots.managing_agency: Town of Holly Springs Parks and Recreation
spots.notes_public: A small 50 acre lake with a two mile loop trail around it. Rentals do not include boards, so bring your own.
spots.rentals: Canoes and rowboats, plus a Gheenoe with a trolling motor. Hirers must be 16 or over. Seven days a week from Memorial Day to Labor Day. No paddleboards listed.

spots.name: Beatty's Ford Access Area
spots.parking_spaces: Large lot with room for long trailers
spots.restrooms: Yes, plus a playground and water play area
spots.notes_public: A hidden gem on the south-western arm of Lake Norman, consistently rated cleaner and less crowded than Blythe Landing. Four wide launch lanes, a playground, picnic areas and a water play area make it a full family outing. No staging dock, so having a partner in the boat for loading helps.

spots.name: Big O's Landing
spots.parking_spaces: Plenty, with room to turn a trailer
spots.restrooms: None. No toilets and no bins.
spots.notes_public: A well built, gentle ramp onto Lake Hickory with generous parking. No facilities at all, and paddlers consistently describe a litter problem. Fine as a put-in, less good as a place to linger.

spots.name: Black Bear Landing
spots.parking_spaces: Plenty, though it fills before midday on fine weekends
spots.hazards: Lake James is a hydroelectric reservoir, so the level rises and falls with power generation. Expect the shoreline and your take-out to look different from one visit to the next.
spots.notes_public: The biggest launch complex on the north side of Lake James, six ramps wide. Open around the clock and busy with trailers, so an early start is worth it. The approach road is winding.

spots.name: Blythe Landing Park
spots.fee_permit: Launch fee applies. Season passes available.
spots.notes_public: A busy trailer ramp with 218 trailer spaces, so expect motorboats. The nonprofit sailing centre on site is the interesting part for paddlers, offering the cheapest membership route onto this lake.
spots.private_launch: Yes for private boats. Only county-approved hire companies may launch commercially.
spots.rentals: Lake Norman Community Sailing, a nonprofit sailing centre, runs from here and its family membership covers kayaking and paddleboarding as well as sailing.

spots.name: Brooks Bridge Paddle Access
spots.hours: Gates are locked at closing. Seasonal hours, roughly 8am to 6pm November to March and later in summer.
spots.hazards: A low head dam sits at this access. Low head dams create a recirculating current below them that is extremely difficult to swim out of. Stay well clear of the face and below it.
spots.low_head_dam: Yes. Paddlers specifically warn about the dam here.
spots.notes_public: The top of the Haw River Paddle Trail and the first point the river is paddleable, with a small waterfall and an island. Quiet, often empty. The dam here deserves real respect.

spots.name: Brown Mountain Beach Resort
spots.camping_type: Cabins, cottages and yurts rather than pitches
spots.hazards: Wilson Creek is a designated Wild and Scenic river with real whitewater upstream. Class rises sharply after rain.
spots.notes_public: Not a public access, so this is one for a night away rather than a day trip. Guests get free use of kayaks, boards and tubes on the creek. Included because Wilson Creek has very little public paddler infrastructure and this is the practical way onto the gentle water.
spots.rentals: Kayaks, paddleboards, floating docks and tubes provided free to guests

spots.name: Buffaloe Road Canoe Launch
spots.managing_agency: City of Raleigh Parks, Recreation and Cultural Resources
spots.walk_to_water: Short, but paddlers describe the bank as steep and awkward for getting a boat in.
spots.hours: Sunrise to sunset. No overnight parking, cars may not be left overnight.
spots.hazards: Steep entry bank. Paddlers report Class I water just below the put-in, which makes paddling back upstream to the car impractical. Plan a downstream take-out.
spots.notes_public: River mile 10.7. Only about five parking spaces. The current just below the launch means this works as a put-in rather than an out-and-back. Roughly four miles downstream to the old Milburnie site at an easy pace.

spots.name: Bynum Dam Access, US 15-501
spots.park_name: Lower Haw River State Natural Area
spots.hazards: Bynum Dam. Put in above the dam only. Never approach a dam face from upstream.
spots.low_head_dam: Yes, Bynum Dam sits immediately downstream of this put-in
spots.flow_high_cfs: 5.7 ft on the Bynum gauge, open-boat limit set by Haw River Assembly
spots.notes_public: Flat for about a mile upstream of the dam, which makes this the gentlest water on the Lower Haw. Stay above the dam.

spots.name: Bynum Mill Access
spots.park_name: Lower Haw River State Natural Area
spots.hazards: Downstream of Bynum Dam. Intermediate to advanced water.
spots.flow_high_cfs: 5.7 ft on the Bynum gauge, open-boat limit set by Haw River Assembly
spots.notes_public: 160 Bynum Church Road. This is the only developed, official paddle launch State Parks maintains in the whole state natural area. Everything else here is undeveloped.

spots.name: Cane Creek Park Lake
spots.camping_type: Drive-in, RV hookups and tent sites plus cabins
spots.notes_public: Not to be confused with the OWASA Cane Creek Reservoir in Orange County. This is Union County's lake near Waxhaw, and it is a very different experience: swimming allowed, paddleboards for hire, camping, disc golf, playgrounds and a mountain bike trail. Residents 65 and over get a free lifetime entry pass.
spots.swimming_allowed: Yes, in the designated swim area
spots.rentals: Canoes, kayaks, paddleboards and pedal boats

spots.name: Cane Creek Reservoir
spots.fee_permit: Orange County residents and OWASA customers: about $6 first person, $2.50 each additional adult, children under 12 and seniors $1. Non-residents: about $10 first person, $4 each additional adult. Private boat launch included in the lake use fee.
spots.hours: Fridays and Saturdays only, 6:30am to 6pm, late March through late October. Closed all other days.
spots.dogs_allowed: No pets within 50 feet of the lake
spots.notes_public: The largest body of water in Orange County and the number one birding hotspot in the county. Strict rules because it is a drinking water reservoir: no paddleboards, no swimming, no body contact with the water at all, no pets near the shoreline, and open only two days a week. Kayaks and canoes are fine and the water is exceptionally clean. Paddlers report it is beautiful and very peaceful. Boats must be inspected on arrival.
spots.swimming_allowed: No. Swimming and all bodily contact with the water are prohibited.
spots.private_launch: Yes, kayaks and canoes only. Paddleboards explicitly prohibited.
spots.rentals: Kayaks, canoes and flat-bottomed boats available for hire on site

spots.name: Copperhead Island
spots.notes_public: A 14 acre island park across the water from McDowell Nature Preserve. Quiet in the morning, busier once the trailers arrive. Six tent sites make it one of very few paddle-and-camp options this close to Charlotte.

spots.name: Cross Point Landing
spots.notes_public: The quieter of the two Wildlife Commission ramps, at the opposite end of the lake from Holleman's Crossing. Plenty of room to manoeuvre.

spots.name: Deep River Park
spots.notes_public: A 40 acre park straddling the Chatham and Lee county line, run by a volunteer association and kept up by the Cumnock community. The historic Camelback Truss Bridge is on the National Register and you can sit on it and watch the river. A clean, easy landing, which paddlers rate more highly than the put-in at Gulf upstream. Picnic tables and a gazebo.
spots.access_type: Private park, open to the public

spots.name: Deep River Rail Trail Trailhead, Franklinville
spots.parking_spaces: Limited, and the entrance is easy to drive past
spots.notes_public: One of the open sections of the Deep River State Trail, a 125 mile hybrid land and paddle trail that will eventually run from High Point to the Haw confluence below Jordan Lake. The rail trail itself is flat, wide and appears wheelchair friendly.

spots.name: Eaton Ferry Marina
spots.hours: Monday to Thursday 9am to 5pm, Friday to Saturday 9am to 7pm, Sunday 9am to 5pm
spots.notes_public: Lake Gaston sits on the Virginia line and is 34 miles long. Eaton Ferry is the primary public-access marina on the NC side, popular with families for pontoon rentals. Not a paddler-focused launch — pontoon and ski boat traffic is heavy — but the only practical entry on this end of the lake without a trailered boat.
spots.rentals: Pontoon boats, ski boats and fishing boats. Military discount available.
spots.access_type: Private marina, open to the public

spots.name: Eno River Access at Red Mill Road
spots.notes_public: Off Red Mill Road near Teknika Parkway in eastern Durham County. Deep flatwater, described as the most accessible launch on the Eno. Two miles upstream to the Little River confluence, two miles down to Falls Lake.

spots.name: Eno River Boat Launch, Red Mill Road
spots.launch_type: Ramp with a new floating dock installed 2022
spots.hazards: Muddy and slippery bank when wet. Use the dock rather than the bank. Road access has had construction detours — check current routing.
spots.notes_public: Flatwater in both directions and genuinely board-friendly. Paddle two miles upstream to the Little River confluence at Penny's Bend or two miles downstream into Falls Lake. Water is deep along most banks. One reviewer explicitly noted paddleboarding here with light motor boat traffic. The 2022 floating dock makes entry and exit much easier than the old muddy bank.

spots.name: Eno River SP, Cabelands Access
spots.hours: 8:30am. Closes 30 minutes before park closing time.
spots.hazards: Swift and often shallow. The river drops one class when levels fall. Downed trees and log jams move with floods and are not always where maps show them.
spots.notes_public: The shortest walk to the Quarry, a popular swimming hole. The gorge section here is rocky and tight — the river is called Cabe's Gorge at this stretch and it rewards a scouting walk before committing to a run. Closed temporarily after flooding events; check before travelling.

spots.name: Eno River SP, Cole Mill Access
spots.hazards: Rapids appear above roughly 2.25 ft on the Eno gauges.
spots.flow_low_cfs: Below 3 ft on the Eno gauges runs shallow
spots.flow_high_cfs: Above 5 ft is beyond most paddlers' ability to self rescue
spots.notes_public: Six miles of trail and a Cole Mill Road gauge nearby, so you can check the level for this exact stretch before driving out.

spots.name: Eno River SP, Cole Mill Access
spots.hours: Cole Mill opens at 9am. Closes 30 minutes before park closing time.
spots.hazards: Swift and often shallow. The river drops one class when levels fall. Downed trees and log jams move with floods and are not always where maps show them.
spots.notes_public: Six miles of trail and the easiest hiking in the park. The Bobbitt Hole swimming hole is reachable from here. Storm damage closed parts of the trail and the suspension bridge as of late 2025 — check current conditions with the park office before travelling.

spots.name: Eno River SP, Fews Ford Access
spots.hazards: Rapids appear above roughly 2.25 ft on the Eno gauges. Swift and often shallow.
spots.flow_low_cfs: Below 3 ft on the Eno gauges runs shallow, harder in a canoe than a kayak
spots.flow_high_cfs: Above 5 ft the river leaves its banks and moves beyond most paddlers' ability to self rescue
spots.notes_public: Visitor centre access with the largest trail network in the park. The park itself describes the Eno as swift but often shallow, which makes paddling here level-dependent rather than reliable.

spots.name: Eno River SP, Pleasant Green Access
spots.parking_spaces: Gravel lot for about 10 to 15 cars, fills quickly at weekends
spots.hours: 8:30am. Closes 30 minutes before park closing time.
spots.hazards: Swift and often shallow. The river drops one class when levels fall. Downed trees and log jams move with floods and are not always where maps show them. The dam at this access was removed, ending the flatwater pool. The river now runs freely and has more current than it did before the removal. Paddling here is no longer suitable as a flatwater out-and-back.
spots.notes_public: Primarily a trail access point rather than a paddling launch since the dam removal. The Laurel Bluffs Trail runs from here, connecting to Pump Station and Cabelands. The parking lot entrance is a sharp right turn immediately after the bridge when travelling from the north — easy to miss.

spots.name: Eno River SP, Pump Station Access
spots.hours: 8am. Closes 30 minutes before park closing time.
spots.hazards: Swift and often shallow. The river drops one class when levels fall. Downed trees and log jams move with floods and are not always where maps show them.
spots.notes_public: The eastern end of the park, with access to the ruins of Durham's first pump station built in 1887. Connects to the Laurel Bluffs Trail and the Mountains-to-Sea Trail. Parking is roadside only with no formal lot.

spots.name: Falls Dam Access
spots.managing_agency: City of Raleigh Parks, Recreation and Cultural Resources
spots.parking_spaces: Car park with double spaces for trailers, plus ADA parking
spots.hours: Sunrise to sunset. No overnight parking, cars may not be left overnight.
spots.hazards: Fast current can push you into downed trees, log jams and bridge footings. The bed is uneven, so never stand where the water is deep enough to float you. Avoid the river in high flow.
spots.notes_public: River mile 0.25 and the top of the Blueway, right below the Falls Lake dam. It is 4.7 miles down to Thornton Road. Flow here depends entirely on what the dam is doing.

spots.name: Falls Lake SRA, B.W. Wells Campground
spots.walk_to_water: Sites 4 and 5 are roughly 300 yards in. Gravel roads mean you can wheel gear down.
spots.fee_permit: Per vehicle at weekends and on holidays in April, May and September, and daily from Memorial Day to Labor Day. Free for day use the rest of the year. Reported at about $7 a car.
spots.restrooms: Yes, flush toilets, showers and charging points
spots.dogs_allowed: Yes, leashed to 6 ft. Not allowed on swim beaches or inside buildings.
spots.hazards: Not every day-use area at Falls Lake opens year round. Check the park's operating season schedule before travelling out of season.
spots.notes_public: Group camping under old, tall, well spaced trees, with shoreline fishing from the farther sites. Mostly out of the RDU flight path, which is not true everywhere on this lake. Site 5 is the furthest and has the best views.

spots.name: Falls Lake SRA, Beaverdam Access
spots.notes_public: The park lists Beaverdam as non-gas boating, which is why it stays calm on a summer weekend. Accessible fishing and swim beach.
spots.private_launch: Yes, at public ramps and designated launch sites only

spots.name: Falls Lake SRA, Highway 50 Access
spots.launch_type: Concrete ramp with a courtesy dock
spots.fee_permit: Per vehicle at weekends and on holidays in April, May and September, and daily from Memorial Day to Labor Day. Free for day use the rest of the year. Reported at about $7 a car.
spots.dogs_allowed: Yes, leashed to 6 ft. Not allowed on swim beaches or inside buildings.
spots.hazards: Not every day-use area at Falls Lake opens year round. Check the park's operating season schedule before travelling out of season.
spots.notes_public: Widely rated the best ramp on Falls Lake: gentle gradient, good grip even wet, and a courtesy dock. The dam dividing Beaverdam Lake from Falls Lake sits here. Note it does not open until 8am, which frustrates anglers wanting a sunrise start.

spots.name: Falls Lake SRA, Rolling View Access
spots.fee_permit: Per vehicle at weekends and on holidays in April, May and September, and daily from Memorial Day to Labor Day. Free for day use the rest of the year. Reported at about $7 a car.
spots.camping_type: Drive-in, with water and 30 amp electric at many sites
spots.dogs_allowed: Yes, leashed to 6 ft. Not allowed on swim beaches or inside buildings.
spots.hazards: Not every day-use area at Falls Lake opens year round. Check the park's operating season schedule before travelling out of season.
spots.notes_public: The most complete access on the lake and the only one with board hire on the doorstep. Swim beach, fishing pier, playground, amphitheatre, and a direct connection to the Mountains-to-Sea Trail. Shady sites, many with a water view.
spots.rentals: A privately owned marina next door hires kayaks, canoes and paddleboards, and has a concession stand, slips and storage.

spots.name: Falls Lake SRA, Sandling Beach Access
spots.launch_type: No boat ramp. Non-motorised craft launch from the beach.
spots.fee_permit: Per vehicle at weekends and on holidays in April, May and September, and daily from Memorial Day to Labor Day. Free for day use the rest of the year. Reported at about $7 a car.
spots.restrooms: Yes, plus showers and changing rooms
spots.motorized_allowed: No, there is no ramp here
spots.dogs_allowed: Yes, leashed to 6 ft. Not allowed on swim beaches or inside buildings.
spots.hazards: Not every day-use area at Falls Lake opens year round. Check the park's operating season schedule before travelling out of season.
spots.notes_public: No ramp, which is exactly why it is worth knowing about. You can carry a board or kayak straight down to the beach with no trailer traffic anywhere near you. Life jackets are available to borrow, and there are picnic shelters, a playground and trails. The far shelters are noticeably quieter.

spots.name: Falls Lake SRA, Shinleaf Access
spots.walk_to_water: Sites run from a short walk to about a mile down a wide gravel then natural path. A trolley or dolly is worth having.
spots.fee_permit: Per vehicle at weekends and on holidays in April, May and September, and daily from Memorial Day to Labor Day. Free for day use the rest of the year. Reported at about $7 a car.
spots.camping_type: Hike-in, no vehicles at the sites and no electricity
spots.dogs_allowed: Yes, leashed to 6 ft. Not allowed on swim beaches or inside buildings.
spots.hazards: Not every day-use area at Falls Lake opens year round. Check the park's operating season schedule before travelling out of season.
spots.notes_public: Hike-in camping with easy water access, and campers are explicitly encouraged to bring kayaks, canoes and boards. No engine noise at the sites, only boats out on the lake. Pick a site at the end of a branch for space and privacy. The path through the campsite area runs 2.8 miles to a narrow point of the lake.

spots.name: Farmer Lake
spots.hours: Wednesday to Friday 7am to 7pm, Saturday 7am to 7pm, Sunday 1pm to 7pm. Closed Monday and Tuesday.
spots.notes_public: A beautiful, very quiet lake in Caswell County that paddlers describe as too big to cover in one visit. Staff are reported as helpful and safety-conscious. A birder's lake — Green Heron and Scarlet Tanager recorded here. Off the beaten path but well worth the drive. Closed Monday and Tuesday.
spots.rentals: Kayaks available for hire on site

spots.name: French Broad River Park
spots.hazards: Hurricane Helene caused major flooding across the French Broad watershed in autumn 2024. The vast majority of accesses have reopened but some amenities and river conditions changed. Check frenchbroadpaddle.com for current status before going.
spots.notes_public: A well-used riverside park and greenway access in Asheville. Good put-in for the urban Asheville section of the French Broad. Dog-friendly with a dog park, walking paths, bike trail connections and a labyrinth. Paddlers report river otters in the early morning, reintroduced after being wiped out by the 1930s and now recovering. Check Helene recovery status.

spots.name: Glencoe Paddle Access
spots.hazards: The shallow rocky sections make good rapids at normal level but are hard work when the river is low. The stretches backed up behind old mill dams stay paddleable in a dry summer.
spots.notes_public: Sits beside the restored Glencoe mill village, with a walking trail and a well liked sunset view. Good upstream paddling to swimming holes cut into the banks over the years.

spots.name: Gorges SP, Frozen Creek Access
spots.hazards: The Horsepasture River drops 2,000 feet over 18 miles and has serious whitewater. The Toxaway crossing at the trail is manageable at around 2.75 ft on the Rosman USGS gauge but dangerous above that. Gorges receives over 80 inches of rain annually and rivers rise fast. The trails here were heavily impacted by Hurricane Helene and cleanup continues as of mid-2026.
spots.notes_public: Temperate rainforest at the NC-SC line with 26 waterfalls and access to part of Lake Jocassee. The Frozen Creek access is the trailhead for the Foothills Trail and the Canebrake Trail to the Toxaway River crossing. Not a paddling destination in the conventional sense — the whitewater here is for experts only. Signage improved post-Helene, no cell service at the far end.

spots.name: Graham Paddle Access
spots.dogs_allowed: Yes, and paddlers report it is a friendly spot for dogs
spots.hazards: The boat ramp is reported to be very slick close to the water. The shallow rocky sections make good rapids at normal level but are hard work when the river is low. The stretches backed up behind old mill dams stay paddleable in a dry summer.
spots.notes_public: A plain access with no facilities at all, but a shady spot for lunch. Staff clear the car park promptly at closing, so do not plan to linger.

spots.name: Great Bend Park
spots.hazards: Paddlers report broken glass on the trails, sharp drops to the water at several points, and poorly maintained access points. There is a dam here. The shallow rocky sections make good rapids at normal level but are hard work when the river is low. The stretches backed up behind old mill dams stay paddleable in a dry summer.
spots.notes_public: Several trails and a tranquil dam, but the park is not well kept and the water access points are the weakest part of it. Restrooms and trail maps at the car park.

spots.name: Greenville Town Common Boat Access
spots.managing_agency: City of Greenville Parks and Recreation
spots.ada_launch: Yes, accessible kayak and canoe launch installed 2018
spots.notes_public: The classic put-in for the 3.5-mile flatwater paddle to Port Terminal. Downtown Greenville's 21-acre riverside park, with an amphitheatre, inclusive playground and the Sycamore Hill Gateway Plaza. Motorized boats are directed to Port Terminal. The kayak and canoe launch is accessible. Paddle tours with Knee Deep Adventures and Riverside Recreation launch from here.

spots.name: Hanging Rock SP, Dan River Access
spots.notes_public: Dedicated paddling access on the Dan, linked to the main park area by the Indian Creek Trail.

spots.name: Hap Simpson River Access Park
spots.hazards: Hurricane Helene caused major flooding across the French Broad watershed in autumn 2024. The vast majority of accesses have reopened but some amenities and river conditions changed. Check frenchbroadpaddle.com for current status before going.
spots.notes_public: Take-out for the classic Westfeldt to Hap Simpson run, 5.5 miles downstream. Shaded picnic tables, paved access and river overlook. Restrooms not confirmed on site — reviewers say no trash bags or poop bags so bring your own.

spots.name: Harris Lake County Park
spots.managing_agency: Wake County Parks, Recreation and Open Space
spots.launch_type: Cartop launch for canoes, kayaks and paddleboards only
spots.walk_to_water: You must unload in the car park and carry your boat 150 yards to the launch. No parking at the water.
spots.fee_permit: None to launch your own boat
spots.motorized_allowed: No. Nothing with a trailer or a motor may launch from inside the park.
spots.notes_public: A 680 acre park on a peninsula of Harris Lake. Note as of early 2026 the cartop launch was closed for construction of a new kayak launch, with paddlers directed to the shore access in the powerline easement near the picnic area. Ring ahead. Trailered and motorised boats have to use the Wildlife Commission ramps elsewhere on the lake.
spots.rentals: None in the park

spots.name: Headwaters Outfitters
spots.hazards: Hurricane Helene caused major flooding across the French Broad watershed in autumn 2024. The vast majority of accesses have reopened but some amenities and river conditions changed. Check frenchbroadpaddle.com for current status before going. Trips cancelled at 3ft on the Rosman USGS gauge.
spots.flow_high_cfs: 3 ft on Rosman gauge — trips cancelled above this level
spots.notes_public: The headwaters section of the French Broad out of Rosman — gentle, lively current with fast-moving shoals and river bends. Highly rated operation with staff handling put-in and take-out. Includes a coffee truck and tap room. One of the most reviewed outfitters in the mountains.
spots.private_launch: Customers only, via private river access 1 mile from shop
spots.rentals: Canoes, kayaks. Self-guided 3-hour and 4 and 7-hour trips on Tuesdays. River trips cancelled at 3ft on the Rosman USGS gauge.

spots.name: Hidden Cove Access
spots.parking_spaces: About 20 trailer-length spaces, and it fills quickly
spots.restrooms: Single vault toilet, no running water
spots.hours: 7am to 9pm, and reported to close seasonally over winter
spots.hazards: Lake James is a hydroelectric reservoir, so the level rises and falls with power generation. Expect the shoreline and your take-out to look different from one visit to the next. Paddlers also report the access closed outside the main season despite listings saying otherwise, so ring the park first.
spots.notes_public: Quieter than the other Lake James ramps because it is easy to drive past. Facilities are primitive but functional. Unlike most access areas here it has posted hours rather than being open around the clock.

spots.name: Holleman's Crossing Boating Access
spots.notes_public: The main trailer ramp on Harris Lake and the launch point for fishing tournaments, so expect bass boats. Ample parking and deep water at the ramp.

spots.name: Jordan Lake SRA, Crosswinds Campground
spots.fee_permit: Per vehicle on weekends and holidays in April, May and September, and daily from Memorial Day to Labor Day
spots.dogs_allowed: Yes, leashed to 6 ft. Not allowed on swim beaches or inside buildings.
spots.notes_public: Boat ramp and swim beach are for campers only. A privately owned marina sits nearby.
spots.private_launch: Yes, at public ramps and designated launch sites only
spots.rentals: Privately owned marina nearby hires fishing boats, kayaks and paddleboards

spots.name: Jordan Lake SRA, Ebenezer Church Access
spots.fee_permit: Per vehicle on weekends and holidays in April, May and September, and daily from Memorial Day to Labor Day
spots.dogs_allowed: Yes, leashed to 6 ft. Not allowed on swim beaches or inside buildings.
spots.notes_public: Named by the park as the best access for windsurfing, which tells you it catches wind. Accessible swim beach and picnic shelters on site.
spots.private_launch: Yes, at public ramps and designated launch sites only

spots.name: Jordan Lake SRA, New Hope Overlook Access
spots.fee_permit: Per vehicle on weekends and holidays in April, May and September, and daily from Memorial Day to Labor Day
spots.dogs_allowed: Yes, leashed to 6 ft. Not allowed on swim beaches or inside buildings.
spots.notes_public: Day-use ramps plus short hike-in backpack camping. The quietest corner of the lake.
spots.private_launch: Yes, at public ramps and designated launch sites only

spots.name: Jordan Lake SRA, Parkers Creek Access
spots.fee_permit: Per vehicle on weekends and holidays in April, May and September, and daily from Memorial Day to Labor Day
spots.dogs_allowed: Yes, leashed to 6 ft. Not allowed on swim beaches or inside buildings.
spots.notes_public: Tent, trailer and RV sites with some hookups, plus walk-up only loops and group camping. Swim beach and picnic shelters.
spots.private_launch: Yes, at public ramps and designated launch sites only

spots.name: Jordan Lake SRA, Poplar Point Campground
spots.fee_permit: Per vehicle on weekends and holidays in April, May and September, and daily from Memorial Day to Labor Day
spots.dogs_allowed: Yes, leashed to 6 ft. Not allowed on swim beaches or inside buildings.
spots.notes_public: Campers-only boat ramp and docks. Walk-up loops mean you can sometimes get a site without booking.
spots.private_launch: Yes, at public ramps and designated launch sites only

spots.name: Jordan Lake SRA, Seaforth Access
spots.fee_permit: Per vehicle on weekends and holidays in April, May and September, and daily from Memorial Day to Labor Day
spots.dogs_allowed: Yes, leashed to 6 ft. Not allowed on swim beaches or inside buildings.
spots.notes_public: Wide open view of the lake, which is scenic and also means very little shelter from wind.
spots.private_launch: Yes, at public ramps and designated launch sites only

spots.name: Jordan Lake SRA, Vista Point Access
spots.fee_permit: Per vehicle on weekends and holidays in April, May and September, and daily from Memorial Day to Labor Day
spots.dogs_allowed: Yes, leashed to 6 ft. Not allowed on swim beaches or inside buildings.
spots.notes_public: Group camping only, both RV and tent. Sailboat launch and swim beach.
spots.private_launch: Yes, at public ramps and designated launch sites only

spots.name: Jordan Lake SRA, White Oak Recreation Area
spots.fee_permit: Per vehicle on weekends and holidays in April, May and September, and daily from Memorial Day to Labor Day
spots.hours: 9am to 5pm weekdays. Closed Saturday and Sunday.
spots.dogs_allowed: Yes, leashed to 6 ft. Not allowed on swim beaches or inside buildings.
spots.notes_public: Open for day use in peak season only when the rental facility is not booked, so call ahead before driving out.
spots.private_launch: Yes, at public ramps and designated launch sites only

spots.name: Jordan Lake, Farrington Point Boat Ramp
spots.launch_type: Four concrete ramps plus a separate hand-carry launch
spots.dogs_allowed: Yes, leashed to 6 ft. Not allowed on swim beaches or inside buildings.
spots.notes_public: The north end of the lake and the busiest tournament ramp on Jordan — nearly every bass tournament launches here because it is free and open around the clock. Four ramps for trailered boats on the right and a separate dedicated launch on the left for canoes and kayaks. Despite the tournament traffic, paddlers say waits rarely exceed ten minutes and are usually none at all.
spots.swimming_allowed: Yes, designated areas elsewhere on the lake
spots.swim_area_here: Small beach area, not a designated swim beach

spots.name: Jordan Lake, Poe's Ridge Boat Ramp
spots.launch_type: Two concrete ramps, one floating pedestrian dock
spots.parking_spaces: Car and trailer parking, limited car-only spaces
spots.fee_permit: Per vehicle on weekends and holidays in April, May and September, and daily from Memorial Day to Labor Day
spots.ada_launch: Yes, ADA accessible aluminum floating dock
spots.dogs_allowed: Yes, leashed to 6 ft. Not allowed on swim beaches or inside buildings.
spots.notes_public: At the south end of the lake near the dam, one of four 24-hour ramps on Jordan. The only one managed by the Army Corps of Engineers rather than NC State Parks or the Wildlife Commission. One lane is blocked by the pedestrian dock placement, so effectively one usable ramp. Paddlers report it is well maintained and monitored. Disabled veterans with a lifetime pass launch free.
spots.swimming_allowed: Yes, designated areas elsewhere on the lake

spots.name: Kerr Lake SRA, Bullocksville Access
spots.notes_public: Accessible fishing pier, concession stand and a short hiking loop. No boat ramp listed by the park.
spots.private_launch: Yes, at public ramps and designated launch sites only

spots.name: Kerr Lake SRA, County Line Access
spots.parking_spaces: Two ramps with parking described as somewhat tight
spots.notes_public: Open sailing water with camping and group sites.
spots.private_launch: Yes, at public ramps and designated launch sites only

spots.name: Kerr Lake SRA, Henderson Point Access
spots.notes_public: Accessible fishing pier and a swim area. Good sailing water, which means it is open and can get choppy.
spots.private_launch: Yes, at public ramps and designated launch sites only

spots.name: Kerr Lake SRA, Hibernia Access
spots.notes_public: Longest trail in the park runs from here, along with a swim area and group camping.
spots.private_launch: Yes, at public ramps and designated launch sites only

spots.name: Kerr Lake SRA, J.C. Cooper Campground
spots.notes_public: Ramp and dock are campers only. Sits within the Satterwhite Point access.
spots.private_launch: Yes, at public ramps and designated launch sites only

spots.name: Kerr Lake SRA, Kimball Point Access
spots.notes_public: Swim beach and camping. Named by the park as good sailing water, so read the wind before you go.
spots.private_launch: Yes, at public ramps and designated launch sites only

spots.name: Kerr Lake SRA, Nutbush Bridge Access
spots.notes_public: Two ramps, one sized for fishing tournaments. Expect heavy trailer traffic on tournament weekends.
spots.private_launch: Yes, at public ramps and designated launch sites only

spots.name: Kerr Lake SRA, Satterwhite Point Access
spots.notes_public: Visitor centre, the park's only designated swim beach, and a privately owned marina. The busiest access on the lake.
spots.swim_area_here: Yes, the only designated swim beach in the park
spots.private_launch: Yes, at public ramps and designated launch sites only

spots.name: Lake Benson Boat House
spots.managing_agency: Town of Garner Parks and Recreation
spots.dogs_allowed: No, pets are not permitted on boathouse craft
spots.notes_public: Worth reading twice before you drive out. You cannot put your own boat on this lake at all, only boathouse craft, and the boathouse opens weekends only. A shallow, quiet lake if you are happy in a hired kayak.
spots.rentals: Jon boats, kayaks and canoes from the boathouse. Trolling motor available.

spots.name: Lake Brandt Marina
spots.managing_agency: City of Greensboro Parks and Recreation
spots.launch_type: Beach launch for paddlecraft, plus a ramp for motorboats
spots.fee_permit: About $6 to $8 per private boat, depending which page you read. An annual launch pass is available. All boaters must register and pay at the marina office.
spots.hours: 7am to 8pm. Closed Tuesday and Wednesday. All boats off the water 30 minutes before closing.
spots.motorized_allowed: Yes, there is a ramp for motorboats
spots.hazards: Closed two days a week, so check before driving.
spots.notes_public: An 816 acre reservoir and the largest of the three Greensboro city lakes to allow boards. Paddlers report the motorboat ramp gets sandy where it meets the kayak beach launch. Weekly night paddles rotate between the three city lakes for ages 13 and up, booking required.
spots.swimming_allowed: No. Swimming and wading are prohibited at all Greensboro city lakes.
spots.rentals: Solo kayak about $15, tandem about $25, paddleboard about $15. Hire runs 1 May to 31 October, first come first served, with no time limit. Renters must be 16 or over. Ages 9 to 15 may paddle a solo boat with a signed waiver and a parent alongside in another boat. Under 9 must share a tandem with an adult. These age rules apply to private boats too.

spots.name: Lake Crabtree County Park
spots.managing_agency: Wake County Parks, Recreation and Open Space
spots.notes_public: Free boat hire, which is rare, and that includes paddleboards. Demand is heavy at weekends and in good weather, so paddlers advise arriving about half an hour before opening.
spots.rentals: Canoes, kayaks, rowboats, pedal boats and paddleboards, free of charge with valid ID

spots.name: Lake Devin
spots.launch_type: Boat ramp plus a separate dedicated kayak launch
spots.notes_public: A lake with two separate access points: a boat ramp and a dedicated kayak launch. Trails are described as overgrown and unmarked in places. A good birding lake — Loons, Grebes, Wilson's Snipe and ducks recorded here. A trail crosses the dam and connects to a wooded loop.

spots.name: Lake Higgins Marina
spots.managing_agency: City of Greensboro Parks and Recreation
spots.fee_permit: About $6 to $8 per private boat, depending which page you read. An annual launch pass is available. All boaters must register and pay at the marina office.
spots.hours: Seasonal, check the marina before setting out
spots.motorized_allowed: Yes, there is a ramp for motorboats
spots.notes_public: At 226 acres this is the smallest and quietest of the Greensboro city lakes, with a hatchery pond and a shoreline trail. The gentler alternative when Brandt and Townsend are busy. Coordinates here are approximate and want checking on the ground.
spots.swimming_allowed: No. Swimming and wading are prohibited at all Greensboro city lakes.
spots.rentals: Solo kayak about $15, tandem about $25, paddleboard about $15, canoe about $25. Higgins is the only one of the three city lakes that hires canoes. Hire runs 1 May to 31 October, first come first served, with no time limit. Renters must be 16 or over. Ages 9 to 15 may paddle a solo boat with a signed waiver and a parent alongside in another boat. Under 9 must share a tandem with an adult. These age rules apply to private boats too.

spots.name: Lake James SP, Catawba River Access
spots.walk_to_water: Campsites are a long walk from the car park, reported as up to a mile and downhill on the way in. Wheelbarrows are provided. The access road may not be used for unloading.
spots.restrooms: Yes, bath house at the car park
spots.hazards: Lake James is a hydroelectric reservoir, so the level rises and falls with power generation. Expect the shoreline and your take-out to look different from one visit to the next.
spots.notes_public: A 24-hour ramp and the easiest put-in for the Long Arm paddle-in campsites. You can boat right up to a lakefront site, and there are lockers at the sites for food. Pack light if you are walking in, because the haul from the car park is a real one.

spots.name: Lake James SP, Paddy's Creek Access
spots.camping_type: Drive-in, 33 sites with parking for two vehicles
spots.dogs_allowed: Yes, leashed to 6 ft. No pets on the beach.
spots.hazards: Lake James is a hydroelectric reservoir, so the level rises and falls with power generation. Expect the shoreline and your take-out to look different from one visit to the next.
spots.notes_public: A rare thing in this dataset: a genuine sandy swim beach with a designated swimming area, backed by Blue Ridge foothills. Launch from the day-use area at the end of Lake James State Park Road for the paddle-in campsites on Long Arm peninsula, about a mile out. Take a free overnight parking pass for the dashboard and park in the top tier of the car park.
spots.swim_area_here: Yes, a large sandy swim beach
spots.rentals: Canoes and kayaks on site

spots.name: Lake Johnson Park
spots.managing_agency: City of Raleigh Parks and Recreation
spots.walk_to_water: Paddlers report hauling boats from the far end of the car park when the near lot fills. Awkward with anything you cannot carry one-handed.
spots.parking_spaces: Two car parks, both of which fill early at weekends
spots.notes_public: A 150 acre lake close to NC State, calm and well liked by beginners. Parking is the real constraint. Arrive early at a weekend or you will be carrying your board a long way.
spots.rentals: Kayaks and paddleboards from WakeRack lockers by the Waterfront Center. Pedal boats, canoes and fishing boats through the park.

spots.name: Lake Mackintosh Marina
spots.managing_agency: City of Burlington Recreation and Parks
spots.hours: 7am to 7:30pm, to 8pm Saturday. Closed Monday and Tuesday.
spots.hazards: Paddlers report submerged stumps and floating logs and debris. Less of a problem on a board than under a propeller, but worth watching in the shallows.
spots.notes_public: The closest Triad lake to Chatham County and well liked by paddlers, with staff who will suggest a route and tell you the distance. Quiet enough that regulars are protective of it. Shoreline is zoned by activity. Bring cash for the launch fee.
spots.rentals: Kayaks, canoes and paddleboards

spots.name: Lake Michie Park and Marina
spots.hours: 6:30am to 6pm Friday through Monday. Closed Tuesday, Wednesday and Thursday.
spots.notes_public: One of the very few launches in the region with an ADA accessible boat house, dock and canoe/kayak launch. Non-motorized only, covering canoes, kayaks, paddleboards and sailboats, so it stays quiet.

spots.name: Lake Norman State Park
spots.notes_public: Largest manmade lake in the state with 520 miles of shoreline. Boat rentals, swim beach and cabins. Check the DEQ algal bloom dashboard here in summer.
spots.private_launch: Yes, at public ramps and designated launch sites only
spots.rentals: Boat hire on site

spots.name: Lake Norman YMCA Lake Access
spots.hours: Lake access is seasonal and limited, historically summer Saturdays only. Ring before going.
spots.notes_public: A supervised cove with lifeguards on the water and life jackets required, which makes it one of the gentlest introductions to a board anywhere on Lake Norman. Equipment is free but you need a Y membership, and lake access hours are far shorter than the building's.
spots.private_launch: Members only. Nationwide YMCA memberships are accepted.
spots.rentals: Canoes, kayaks and paddleboards provided free to members, plus inflatables in the cove

spots.name: Lake Thom-A-Lex Park
spots.ada_launch: Yes, the launch is described as accessible
spots.notes_public: Shared by Thomasville and Lexington, hence the name. An accessible launch, trailer parking and a bait shop, with a lakeside walking trail and plenty of shoreline.

spots.name: Lake Townsend Marina
spots.managing_agency: City of Greensboro Parks and Recreation
spots.launch_type: Large boat ramp plus a separate ramp for small sailboats
spots.fee_permit: About $6 to $8 per private boat, depending which page you read. An annual launch pass is available. All boaters must register and pay at the marina office.
spots.ada_launch: No, but the fishing pier, parking and restrooms are reachable with a mobility device
spots.hours: 7am to 8pm. Closed Wednesday and Thursday. All boats off the water 30 minutes before closing.
spots.motorized_allowed: Yes, there is a ramp for motorboats
spots.hazards: Closed two days a week.
spots.notes_public: Greensboro's largest municipal reservoir and home to the Lake Townsend Yacht Club, which is open to the public and does not require you to own a boat. Open sailing water, so read the wind. Bring your own board, since hire here is kayaks and rowboats only.
spots.swimming_allowed: No. Swimming and wading are prohibited at all Greensboro city lakes.
spots.rentals: Solo kayak about $15, tandem about $25, and rowboats. No paddleboard hire listed here, unlike Brandt and Higgins. Sailboats can be hired with prior experience. Hire runs 1 May to 31 October, first come first served, with no time limit. Renters must be 16 or over. Ages 9 to 15 may paddle a solo boat with a signed waiver and a parent alongside in another boat. Under 9 must share a tandem with an adult. These age rules apply to private boats too.

spots.name: Lake Wheeler Park
spots.managing_agency: City of Raleigh Parks and Recreation
spots.launch_type: Ramp for trailered and hand-carried boats
spots.fee_permit: Daily or annual launch pass required, about $6 a day for non-residents
spots.hours: 6am to 8pm. Boats must be off the water 30 minutes before sunset or closing, whichever is first.
spots.motorized_allowed: Yes, no jet skis. 40 mph limit, and skiing and tubing are permitted.
spots.notes_public: A 650 acre water supply lake, and the clearest example of flat water that is not swimmable. Swimming and wading are both banned, and motorboats can run at 40 mph with skiers behind them. Fine for a confident paddler, a poor choice for a first time on a board.
spots.swimming_allowed: No. Swimming and wading are both prohibited.
spots.rentals: Kayaks and paddleboards from WakeRack self-service lockers near the Waterfront Center, booked online

spots.name: Latta Nature Preserve
spots.notes_public: Mountain Island Lake is smaller and far less trafficked than Lake Norman, with much less motor traffic. Forested and undeveloped, and a good choice when the big lake is churned up.
spots.rentals: Mountain Island Lake Paddle Company will deliver boards and kayaks to the launches

spots.name: Lilly's Bridge Marina
spots.hours: Tuesday to Thursday 10am to 4pm, Friday 10am to 4pm, Saturday 10am to 5:30pm, Sunday 12:30 to 5:30pm. Closed Monday.
spots.notes_public: A full-service marina on the south arm of Lake Tillery with a restaurant, mini-golf and a boat ramp open to the public. Rated the favourite launch on the lake by regular paddlers. Closed Monday.
spots.rentals: Kayaks and paddleboard hire, plus pontoon boats. Restaurant on site.
spots.access_type: Private marina, open to the public

spots.name: Little River Fishing Facility
spots.hours: 6:30am to 6pm Monday, Friday, Saturday and Sunday. Closed Tuesday, Wednesday and Thursday.
spots.notes_public: Rental only, like Lake Benson. You cannot launch your own boat here, and it is shut three days a week. Restrooms on site, no bait sold.
spots.private_launch: No. Hired craft only, and private trolling motors are not permitted.
spots.rentals: Kayaks, canoes and jon boats with trolling motors. Bring your own battery.

spots.name: Lumber River SP, Chalk Banks Access
spots.notes_public: The Lumber is a Wild and Scenic river and one of the darkest blackwater rivers in the Southeast — tannin-stained and deeply remote. Chalk Banks is the main access on the upper river, with picnic grills and a riverside trail. No swimming due to snags, currents and the remoteness. Security patrol keeps the park clean. Terrain on the trail is rough.

spots.name: Mayo River SP, Anglin Mill Access
spots.notes_public: Mayo Beach and the Boiling Hole are here. No restrooms, so plan around that.

spots.name: Mayo River SP, Mayodan Access
spots.notes_public: Put in on the Mayo and paddle down into the Dan.

spots.name: McDowell Nature Preserve
spots.camping_type: Drive-in, small RV area with electric and water
spots.notes_public: One of the few Mecklenburg sites that explicitly welcomes your own board, launching from the landing by the waterfront deck. Nature centre, forested trails and quiet lake views.
spots.private_launch: Yes, bring your own canoe, kayak or paddleboard
spots.rentals: None for hire, but guided programmes provide boats

spots.name: Medoc Mountain State Park
spots.notes_public: The park calls this one of the cleanest streams in the region. Quiet paddling with almost no boat traffic.
spots.private_launch: Yes, at public ramps and designated launch sites only

spots.name: Merchants Millpond State Park
spots.notes_public: One of the finest paddling destinations in North Carolina, full stop. A blackwater millpond under a canopy of bald cypress and tupelo gum draped with Spanish moss — one reviewer called it his favourite park for over 30 years and noted the cell service is essentially nonexistent. No motors, no crowds, no glamping. Canoe-in primitive camping takes you deep into the swamp. Bring your own boat — no hire on site confirmed. Cell service is very limited.

spots.name: Morrow Mountain State Park
spots.notes_public: Sits where Lake Tillery meets the Yadkin, under the Uwharrie peaks. Boat rentals on site and bald eagles overhead.
spots.private_launch: Yes, at public ramps and designated launch sites only
spots.rentals: Boat hire on site

spots.name: Mt Holly Boat Landing
spots.managing_agency: Privately owned, Aquatic Adventures operates from here
spots.fee_permit: About $2 per person to launch a boat, canoe or kayak
spots.hazards: Sits just below the Mountain Island Lake dam. Flow changes when the dam releases.
spots.notes_public: Private land, and worth every bit of the two dollars. Just south of the Mountain Island dam on a wide, quiet stretch. The run downstream is about 2.75 miles through tree-lined water with almost no development or boat traffic. Rocks show through when the current is up.
spots.private_launch: Yes, for a small per person fee
spots.rentals: Kayaks and paddleboards on site. Aquatic Adventures runs guided trips and full moon paddles from here.

spots.name: Neuse Adventures
spots.notes_public: A well-reviewed outfitter on the Neuse between Falls Lake and Smithfield. Staff handle put-in and take-out, making it a good option for a first river trip. Paddlers consistently mention wildlife — beavers, kingfishers, herons. Owner-operated and described as extremely attentive.
spots.rentals: Canoes and kayaks with shuttle service. Two-hour and five-mile float options.

spots.name: New River SP, Elk Shoals Access
spots.restrooms: None at the access, chapel nearby
spots.notes_public: The only access on the New River with a swim beach and the most popular in summer. Shallow, clear water excellent for families with young children. Gate occasionally closed without notice — reviewers report driving out to find it shut. Call the park office before making the trip.
spots.swimming_allowed: Yes, Elk Shoals has a sandy beach swim area

spots.name: New River SP, Kings Creek Access
spots.notes_public: Parking access for the Alleghany paddle-in only campground downstream. Reviewers call this their favourite campsite on the river, with primitive sites directly on the water. The Alleghany access itself is reachable only by canoe or kayak from here.

spots.name: New River SP, US 221 Access and Visitor Center
spots.camping_type: Drive-in, RV hookups and primitive sites
spots.notes_public: The main visitor centre and one of the two primary car-launch accesses on the New River. The river here is shallow, gentle Class I, ideal for beginners and families. The park covers 26.5 miles of one of the oldest rivers on Earth — more than a billion years old, older than the Appalachian Mountains that surround it. Hellbender salamanders, the largest in the US, live in the river. Park offers shuttle connections to tube and kayak rental providers.
spots.swimming_allowed: Yes, at Elk Shoals access area
spots.swim_area_here: No, swim beach is at Elk Shoals

spots.name: New River SP, Wagoner Road Access
spots.walk_to_water: Sites vary. Hand carts provided to move gear to riverside sites.
spots.notes_public: The second primary car-launch, eight miles southeast of Jefferson. Hand carts are provided at the campground for gear transport to riverside sites. Paddle-in campsites available from here. The river at Wagoner is especially gentle and suitable for all skill levels.

spots.name: Oak Hollow Marina
spots.managing_agency: City of High Point Parks and Recreation
spots.camping_type: Large campground, over 100 RV sites with hookups and some tent spaces
spots.notes_public: The most developed lake in the Triad, with a campground, golf course, sailing club and an open air stage. It also permits water skiing, so the wake is real. Swimming is not allowed. One of very few Triad spots where you can camp and paddle in the same trip.
spots.rentals: Kayaks solo and tandem, paddleboards and sailboats

spots.name: Old Bynum Bridge Access
spots.park_name: Lower Haw River State Natural Area
spots.hazards: Downstream of Bynum Dam. Intermediate to advanced water.
spots.flow_high_cfs: 5.7 ft on the Bynum gauge, open-boat limit set by Haw River Assembly
spots.notes_public: Parking on the east side of Bynum Road. Downstream from here to US 64 is rated by the state natural area for intermediate to advanced paddlers only.

spots.name: Pettigrew State Park, Lake Phelps
spots.notes_public: Lake Phelps is one of the oldest and deepest natural lakes in North Carolina and is described by regular visitors as a hidden gem. The park is the third least visited in the state system. Water levels were significantly down in the 2026 drought — check with the park before making the trip. Under construction as of mid-2026 but trails remain open. Excellent birding.

spots.name: Pilot Mountain SP, Ivy Bluff Access
spots.walk_to_water: Roughly half a mile of trail from the car park down to the river. Smooth surface and a gradual slope, but a long way with a hard board or a canoe on your shoulder.
spots.notes_public: Parking for paddle-in campers, with steep riverside slopes on the hiking approach.

spots.name: Pilot Mountain SP, Shoals Fishing Area
spots.notes_public: Paddling launch for the Yadkin, doubling as a fishing access.

spots.name: Piney Bluff Boat Launch
spots.parking_spaces: Good parking, though it fills at busy times
spots.notes_public: The main launch on Belews Lake, north of Winston-Salem and Greensboro. Popular with jet skis and party boats, so pick your day. Open around the clock.

spots.name: Poole Road Access
spots.managing_agency: City of Raleigh Parks, Recreation and Cultural Resources
spots.parking_spaces: Car park with double spaces for trailers
spots.hours: Sunrise to sunset. No overnight parking, cars may not be left overnight.
spots.hazards: Fast current can push you into downed trees, log jams and bridge footings. The bed is uneven, so never stand where the water is deep enough to float you. Avoid the river in high flow.
spots.notes_public: River mile 17.7 and the downstream end of the Raleigh section. A gravel road just before the river bridge leads in.

spots.name: Port Terminal Boat Access
spots.ada_launch: Yes, dedicated ADA-accessible kayak launch added 2023, built by Sound Rivers
spots.notes_public: The downstream take-out for the classic 3.5-mile Greenville Town Common to Port Terminal flatwater paddle. Old-growth trees line the banks with shifting sandbars that appear seasonally. Only twenty minutes by motorboat to Washington NC's waterfront. Two ramps and a dock. Reviewers note no restrooms on site.

spots.name: Ramseur Lake
spots.hours: Wednesday to Friday 7am to 8pm, Saturday 7am to 8pm, Sunday 8am to 7pm. Closed Monday and Tuesday.
spots.notes_public: A quiet town lake on a branch of the Deep River, with improved docks and a fishing pier. Staff described by reviewers as friendly and attentive. No pets allowed, which one reviewer found listed as dog-friendly online and then discovered was wrong on arrival — worth confirming before bringing dogs.
spots.rentals: None confirmed

spots.name: Ramsey Creek Park
spots.ada_launch: No, but there is an ADA compliant fishing pier
spots.dogs_allowed: Yes, there is a dog park at the entrance
spots.notes_public: A seasonal lifeguarded beach, four ramps and a dog park. The shoreline is rocky, so water shoes help. Check beach dates before relying on it.

spots.name: Randleman Regional Reservoir Marina
spots.fee_permit: Ramp fee applies, staffed check-in station
spots.hours: 6am to 8pm. Closed Monday and Tuesday. Paddlers report it often opens nearer 7am.
spots.notes_public: A large, relatively new drinking water reservoir with good fishing. Tightly regulated: no swimming, no entering the water, closed two days a week and crowded at weekends. Flat and paddleable, but not a lake to fall into by choice.
spots.swimming_allowed: No. Entering the water at all is prohibited, as this is a drinking water reservoir.

spots.name: Raven Rock State Park
spots.notes_public: The park explicitly names rapids on the Cape Fear here, plus the remains of the Northington Lock and Dam. Scout before you run it and check the class rating against current flow.
spots.private_launch: Yes, at public ramps and designated launch sites only

spots.name: River Bend Park Access
spots.managing_agency: City of Raleigh Parks, Recreation and Cultural Resources
spots.parking_spaces: Car park with double spaces for trailers, plus ADA parking
spots.hazards: Fast current can push you into downed trees, log jams and bridge footings. The bed is uneven, so never stand where the water is deep enough to float you. Avoid the river in high flow.
spots.notes_public: River mile 10, and the best equipped access on the Blueway. Restrooms and a changing area, which none of the others have. Only a mile down to Buffaloe Road.

spots.name: River Park North
spots.managing_agency: City of Greenville Parks and Recreation
spots.fee_permit: None for trails and river access. Fishing requires a permit. $2 donation for some programmes.
spots.camping_type: Primitive river-access sites plus drive-to sites
spots.notes_public: An 18-acre park on the Tar with fishing ponds, nature trails, a science centre and paddle boats on the ponds. River access connects to the Tar-Pamlico Water Trail. Three primitive camping platforms on the river, closed in summer due to insects near the swamp — ring ahead. Over a mile of trail from the entrance to the Tar River itself.
spots.swimming_allowed: No, not recommended in the river

spots.name: Roanoke River Boardwalk and Boat Ramp
spots.notes_public: An 18-acre county park built around Williamston's original wharf on the Roanoke. One reviewer launches a 28-foot boat here, so the ramp handles range. ADA accessible boardwalk and restrooms with showers — unusual for a rural access. A riverside camping platform is available for overnight paddlers. Less than a mile to downtown Williamston.

spots.name: Robertson Millpond Preserve
spots.managing_agency: Wake County Parks, Recreation and Open Space
spots.launch_type: Loading dock for canoes, kayaks and boards
spots.fee_permit: None to launch your own boat
spots.hazards: Shallow stretches that are awkward on a board, and water levels drop noticeably in drought.
spots.low_head_dam: Yes, the historic mill dam. The pond is deeper near it.
spots.notes_public: The only blackwater cypress swamp in Wake County and quite unlike anything else near Raleigh. A marked paddling trail loops in about an hour, mixing open water with tight passages through the cypress. Some sections are shallow enough to be tricky on a board.
spots.rentals: Kayak hire on Saturdays only

spots.name: Robeson Creek Boat Ramp
spots.flow_high_cfs: 5.7 ft on the Bynum gauge, open-boat limit set by Haw River Assembly
spots.notes_public: A full trailer ramp run by the Wildlife Resources Commission, so expect motorboats. Paddle about a mile down Robeson Creek to reach the Haw.

spots.name: Robeson Creek Canoe Access
spots.park_name: Lower Haw River State Natural Area
spots.flow_high_cfs: 5.7 ft on the Bynum gauge, open-boat limit set by Haw River Assembly
spots.notes_public: Despite the name this launch is on the Haw, not on Robeson Creek. Flat for a short way upstream and flat for a long way downstream all the way to Jordan Lake, which makes it the best board-friendly put-in on the Lower Haw.

spots.name: Salem Lake Marina Center
spots.managing_agency: City of Winston-Salem Recreation and Parks
spots.restrooms: Yes, ADA compliant at the marina and part way round the trail
spots.motorized_allowed: Yes, up to 60 horsepower. No jet skis and no pleasure boating.
spots.notes_public: Over 350 acres inside the city limits, and the horsepower cap plus the jet ski ban make it far calmer than its size suggests. A seven mile dirt trail rings the lake.
spots.rentals: Boat hire from the marina centre, which also holds the fishing station and bait shop

spots.name: Saxapahaw Lake Paddle Access
spots.launch_type: Dock, with a life jacket loaner station
spots.walk_to_water: Carry your boat from the car to the dock, then park in the main lot or at the Boy Scout camp nearby. Short carry, described as very manageable.
spots.notes_public: Flat water behind the old mill dam, which makes this the gentlest put-in on the whole Haw and the one to pick for a first river paddle or a low water summer day. Out-and-back paddling with herons, egrets and a beaver dam. Walking trails, a playground and food within a short walk, plus a kayak shop nearby. The Haw Mill Race below the spillway is a different proposition entirely.

spots.name: Shallow Ford Natural Area
spots.launch_type: Paddle boat slip from a gravel car park
spots.walk_to_water: A second access sits down the Homestead Trail with a steep climb down to the water. Wear proper shoes and think twice with a hard board.
spots.hours: Gates are locked at closing. Seasonal hours, roughly 8am to 6pm November to March and later in summer.
spots.hazards: Fast flowing water and a steep bank at the trail access. The shallow rocky sections make good rapids at normal level but are hard work when the river is low. The stretches backed up behind old mill dams stay paddleable in a dry summer.
spots.notes_public: Multiple river access points, several miles of well marked trail and primitive camping, on a section of the Mountains-to-Sea Trail. One of the few Haw accesses where you can stay the night.
spots.swimming_allowed: Not advised. Paddlers describe the river here as muddy and fast flowing.

spots.name: Smithfield Town Commons
spots.route_name: Neuse River Blueway, Johnston County section
spots.notes_public: One of only two established Neuse accesses in Johnston County, the other being near Richardson Bridge at Princeton. A riverside park with a paved path, in the town centre. Smithfield is the start of the 170 mile Mountains-to-Sea paddle route to the Croatan.

spots.name: South Bynum River Access
spots.walk_to_water: Long. The recommended approach is to park on the east side of the historic Bynum Bridge and walk across it, which is a real haul with a canoe or a hard board.
spots.park_name: Lower Haw River State Natural Area
spots.hazards: Downstream of Bynum Dam. Intermediate to advanced water.
spots.flow_high_cfs: 5.7 ft on the Bynum gauge, open-boat limit set by Haw River Assembly
spots.notes_public: Formerly Bynum Beach Canoe Access. Parking is extremely limited and roadside parking on Bynum Beach Road is expressly prohibited, so plan on the bridge walk with your board.

spots.name: South Mountains SP, Clear Creek Access
spots.hazards: Reported closed for construction of a new car park from 31 March 2026, possibly until the end of the year, with no parking and no trespassing signs posted. Confirm with the park office before travelling.
spots.notes_public: A day-use access on Clear Creek with a pond, picnic area and restrooms at the trailhead, and a trail running beside the water. Shallow in places. Check it has reopened before you make the drive.

spots.name: Southmont Abbotts Creek Boat Access
spots.notes_public: High Rock is the second largest lake in the state and, unusually for this region, has a designated swim area elsewhere on the water. Paddlers rate this access as markedly less crowded than Norman or Wylie, with shoreline fishing and walking trails.

spots.name: Stone Mountain State Park
spots.camping_type: Drive-in with hookups and primitive sites
spots.notes_public: A spectacular granite dome rising 600 feet above the surrounding terrain — one of the most visited state parks in NC. The Roaring River runs through the park with trout fishing and creek paddling. No cell service in most of the park. Upper sections of the river are for experienced paddlers. The lower section near the homestead is gentler.

spots.name: Sunset Park Boat Ramp
spots.hours: 1pm to 7pm Monday to Friday, 1pm to 7pm Saturday, 1pm to 5pm Sunday
spots.route_name: Tar River Paddle Trail, Upper Tar section
spots.hazards: Davenport grist mill dam sits about 1.25 miles downstream from the Reservoir Dam access upstream. Portage on river right. The dam area is private property — stay in the boat.
spots.notes_public: One of the Upper Tar section access points on the Tar River Paddle Trail, which connects 55 miles of river across ten launches. From here downstream the Tar becomes increasingly flatwater. Tar River Life in nearby Bunn offers kayak rentals and shuttle services if you need them.

spots.name: Swepsonville River Park, Lower Access
spots.hours: Gates are locked at closing. Seasonal hours, roughly 8am to 6pm November to March and later in summer.
spots.hazards: The shallow rocky sections make good rapids at normal level but are hard work when the river is low. The stretches backed up behind old mill dams stay paddleable in a dry summer.
spots.notes_public: Calm water and a good put-in. From the lower access you can run downstream toward Saxapahaw or turn up Great Alamance Creek. Popular with bank anglers, so the parking goes quickly.

spots.name: Swift Island Access Area
spots.notes_public: A quiet Wildlife Commission ramp on Lake Tillery with a boardwalk and family-friendly shoreline. Reviewers describe a peaceful Sunday-afternoon feel with trucks and trailers but enough room to move. One of the calmer ends of a large lake.

spots.name: Tailrace Marina
spots.notes_public: Near the mouth of Dutchman's Creek where it meets Lake Wylie. Online booking and waivers mean you can be on the water quickly. A long-standing Catawba Riverkeeper Riversweep site.
spots.rentals: Kayaks, paddleboards, canoes and pontoons. An annual kayak membership covers a guest.

spots.name: Tar River Reservoir Boat Ramp
spots.route_name: Tar River Paddle Trail, Nash County section
spots.notes_public: Free 24-hour ramp at the upper reservoir. A quiet, remote flatwater stretch above the main Rocky Mount section, with occasional motorboat traffic. Jacob's Swamp at river mile 93 is accessible by a small cut on river left.

spots.name: Thornton Road Access
spots.managing_agency: City of Raleigh Parks, Recreation and Cultural Resources
spots.walk_to_water: Half a mile down the paved greenway. Carry your boat to the T junction, turn right and walk a short way further. A serious haul with a canoe or hard board.
spots.hours: Sunrise to sunset. No overnight parking, cars may not be left overnight.
spots.hazards: Fast current can push you into downed trees, log jams and bridge footings. The bed is uneven, so never stand where the water is deep enough to float you. Avoid the river in high flow.
spots.notes_public: River mile 4.5. The longest carry on the Blueway by a wide margin, so worth knowing before you load the car. Signs mark the access once you reach the greenway.

spots.name: U.S. National Whitewater Center
spots.fee_permit: Around $39 for a day of flatwater kayaking and paddleboarding, plus about $13 to park
spots.notes_public: The flatwater paddling here is on the Catawba and Long Creek and is separate from the artificial whitewater channel. Everything is an added fee, so read the pricing before you go.
spots.private_launch: Unknown, the site is built around its own hire fleet
spots.rentals: Flatwater kayaks and paddleboards included in the activity pass. Life jacket provided.

spots.name: US 64 Haw River Canoe Access
spots.parking_spaces: Large gravel lot at 348 River Access Road, plus a very small gravel lot on the south east side and roadside parking on the north west service road
spots.park_name: Lower Haw River State Natural Area
spots.hazards: The state natural area rates the run downstream of here for experts only.
spots.flow_high_cfs: 5.7 ft on the Bynum gauge, open-boat limit set by Haw River Assembly
spots.notes_public: Experts only heading downstream toward Robeson Creek. The classic Lower Haw whitewater run starts here and it is not a beginner stretch.

spots.name: University Lake
spots.fee_permit: Orange County residents and OWASA customers: about $6 first person, $2.50 each additional adult, children under 12 and seniors $1. Non-residents: about $10 first person, $4 each additional adult. Private boat launch included in the lake use fee.
spots.hours: Fridays, Saturdays and Sundays, 6:30am to 6pm, late March through late October.
spots.dogs_allowed: No pets within 50 feet of the lake
spots.notes_public: Smaller than Cane Creek and closer to Chapel Hill. Opens on Sundays unlike Cane Creek, which makes it the more accessible of the two for a weekend paddle. Same rules apply: no boards, no swimming, no pets at the shore. Quieter crowd and a more sheltered lake.
spots.swimming_allowed: No. Swimming and all bodily contact with the water are prohibited.
spots.private_launch: Yes, kayaks and canoes only. Paddleboards explicitly prohibited.
spots.rentals: Kayaks, canoes and flat-bottomed boats available for hire

spots.name: Uwharrie River Low Water Bridge Access
spots.managing_agency: US Forest Service, Uwharrie National Forest
spots.hazards: The low water bridge itself floods after heavy rain, sometimes impassably. Check before driving down the gravel road, which has no turnaround. River rises fast in the gorge.
spots.notes_public: The Uwharrie runs through a National Forest gorge with no development visible from the water. Paddlers report wide stairs from the parking area down to the river and room to splash around. The road in is gravel and the bridge floods — check conditions before driving out. Some locals pan for gold here.

spots.name: Valdese Lakeside Park
spots.ada_launch: Yes, the ramp is wide enough for a manual wheelchair or a power scooter
spots.hours: 7am to 8pm, and to 11pm on Friday and Saturday
spots.dogs_allowed: Yes, there is a fenced dog park and water at the gate
spots.notes_public: Lake Rhodhiss is the quieter, more intimate paddling water in Burke County, and this is the best entry to it. A waterfront boardwalk, a suspension bridge and about 12 miles of trail, with a view of Table Rock at sunset. One of only a handful of accessible launches in the whole dataset.
spots.rentals: RAD Rentals will deliver kayaks and paddleboards direct to the dock

spots.name: West Point on the Eno
spots.hazards: Mill dam at the historic mill. Put in above the dam.
spots.low_head_dam: Yes, the mill dam. Launch above it.
spots.notes_public: Enter above the dam behind the mill and paddle roughly three quarters of a mile up to Sennet Hole. The dam holds deep water year round, so this is one of the few Eno spots that does not depend on rain.

spots.name: Westfeldt Park
spots.hazards: Hurricane Helene caused major flooding across the French Broad watershed in autumn 2024. The vast majority of accesses have reopened but some amenities and river conditions changed. Check frenchbroadpaddle.com for current status before going.
spots.notes_public: Put-in for the most-paddled stretch in Henderson County, 5.5 miles of Class I to Hap Simpson Park in Fletcher. Lazy Otter Outfitters operates from here with single kayaks, tandem kayaks, SUPs and tubes, including a horseshoe bend 4-mile trip option. Check Helene recovery status.

spots.name: William B. Umstead SP, Crabtree Creek Access
spots.notes_public: Big Lake and Sycamore Lake, with boat rentals on site. Nine miles from downtown Raleigh and it feels much further.
spots.private_launch: Yes, at public ramps and designated launch sites only
spots.rentals: Boat hire on site

spots.name: William B. Umstead SP, Reedy Creek Access
spots.notes_public: Small lake with a millstone marker from an old grist mill. Group campsites and a stone-deck picnic shelter.
spots.private_launch: Yes, at public ramps and designated launch sites only
